Commentary.Commentary: We are back! A tough task awaits for Bangladesh as their openers, Mahmudul Hasan Joy and Shadman Islam make their way out to the middle now. We can see the South African players taking their respective field positions. As Kyle Verreynne was cramping up while batting and spent a long time, it will be Ryan Rickelton to take up the wicket-keeping duties. Kagiso Rabada has the new ball in hand and is raring to go. Let's play...
... THIRD INNINGS ...

Bangladesh started well with the ball with Hasan Mahmud picking up a wicket in the very first over. They also managed to keep picking up wickets at regular intervals with Taijul Islam starring with a fine five-wicket haul to have South Africa to 108/6. However, they were pretty disappointing from the start of Day 2 and the ball being old also didn't help. They allowed the Proteas to take the game away from them, but Hasan Mahmud did manage to break it just before Lunch and added another the very next ball to see an opening. But they struggled once again to wrap things up as the Proteas tail wagged and wagged long enough which cost them runs and now they need something extraordinary to first diminish this mammoth lead and then set up a target that could trouble the visitors. Join us in a bit to see how things pan out.

South Africa have batted brilliantly to take a massive lead of 202 runs as they end the inning at 308 runs. Kyle Verreynne was the star of the show with an incredible ton and was involved in a couple of important partnerships that got them well ahead in the game. Initially, it was Tony de Zorzi and Tristan Stubbs who steadied the ship but batting was not easy at all on the first day. However, that big 119-run partnership between Kyle Verreynne and Wiaan Mulder where the latter notched up his maiden Test half-century as well helped the Proteas extend the lead further. Dane Piedt also played an important part in frustrating the bowlers and adding over 50 runs with the centurion, and putting even more pressure on the hosts.

Commentary.Commentary: We are back! The umpires make their way out to the middle and are followed by Bangladesh fielders who are spreading across the field. Kyle Verreynne and Dane Piedt are ready to resume their stay at the crease. Taijul Islam will start the proceedings with the ball this session. Away we go!
... DAY 2, SESSION 2 ...

Then came Hasan Mahmud, delivering a much-needed spark for the hosts. Using reverse swing to deadly effect, he shattered the partnership with a crucial breakthrough, dismissing Mulder. And as if that wasn’t enough, he followed it up with a great delivery on the very next ball, sending Keshav Maharaj’s stumps flying and reigniting Bangladesh's hopes. The sudden shift in momentum injected fresh energy into the hosts, lifting both spirits and intensity on the field. However, Kyle Verreynne stood firm, showing maturity. Partnering with Dane Piedt, he calmly navigated the remainder of the session, ensuring South Africa reached Lunch without further setbacks. With the game well set, we are in for another intriguing session coming up in about 40 minutes.

The way the game unfolded on the opening day, few would have predicted batters to thrive on this tricky surface. But Kyle Verreynne and Wiaan Mulder had other ideas. They stepped out with purpose and confidence, taking charge from the get-go this morning. With nimble footwork and a dazzling array of sweeps and reverse sweeps, they made the pitch look far less menacing than anyone had imagined. Bangladesh, meanwhile, struggled to find their rhythm with the ball. Defensive tactics, including scattered in-out fields, and a dropped catch from Mominul Haque only allowed the partnership to flourish, building pressure on the hosts. Kyle Verreynne and Wiaan Mulder capitalized on every opportunity, reaching well-crafted half-centuries and leaving the Bangladesh camp visibly deflated as body language began to falter.

SESSION SUMMARY - 30 Overs, 103 Runs and 2 Wickets! What a session we’ve witnessed!  South Africa now lead by 137 runs and Kyle Verreynne is still out there at 77(105)! South Africa certainly dominated the proceedings on Day 2, applying pressure with proactive batting and steadily building a substantial lead. The scoreboard pressure is mounting on Bangladesh as the Proteas extend their advantage. However, just before Lunch, Bangladesh managed to pick up two quick wickets, offering a glimmer of hope and a chance to claw back into the game. Despite that brief setback, South Africa will head into Lunch mighty pleased with their efforts, firmly in control and looking to pile on more runs in the next session.

Commentary.Commentary: We are ready for the game to get underway on Day 2! The umpires and the players are all making their way out to the middle. Wiaan Mulder and Kyle Verreynne are marking their strides and will resume their stay at the crease for South Africa! Taijul Islam will start with the ball for Bangladesh! Here we go!

Bangladesh, however, will see the first hour as a crucial opportunity to clean up the remaining wickets and get back into the game. Though their decision to play just one pacer initially seemed to have backfired, the spinners, led by Taijul Islam, brought them right back into the contest. The surface hasn’t been spitting demons, but offers something for both pacers and spinners, setting the stage for a great battle between bat and ball. With everything at stake, both teams will be eager to take control on this pivotal day, which only promises another thrilling chapter of red-ball cricket. Stay tuned, the action isn’t far away!

After skittling out Bangladesh for just 106, the Proteas missed a chance to fully capitalize but still find themselves in a decent position. With Kyle Verreynne looking composed at the crease, they’ll aim to push their lead by at least 70-80 runs, which could be decisive given the way the surface has behaved so far. Wiaan Mulder has also looked very confident in his approach and South Africa will be hopeful for this partnership to flourish.

Hello and welcome to Day 2 of the first Test between Bangladesh and South Africa at the Shere Bangla National Stadium, Dhaka! The opening day raced along, with South Africa nudging ahead by taking a 34-run lead. With the match moving at such a quick pace, it’s safe to say we could have a clear picture of the outcome by the end of today, or perhaps, the game might even conclude by stumps!
... DAY 2, SESSION 1 ...

Right then, that is it from a thrilling Day 1 of this first Test. South Africa are slightly ahead in this game but Bangladesh have done well not to let them get away with it. Day 2 promises to be another exciting one with these two sides battling hard and we could even get a clear picture of where this game is heading by the end of it. All the action is scheduled to start at 4 am GMT, but as we have lost a few overs, it may begin a bit early as well, and you can also enjoy all the build-up. Cheers!

South Africa knew that batting would be hard and got off to the worst possible start losing skipper Aiden Markram in the first over. However, Tony de Zorzi held one end solidly and steadied the ship, first with Tristan Stubbs and then with David Bedingham. But none of his partners could stay for long finding it tough against the spinners. Ryan Rickelton came out and tried to be proactive, which worked as he scored 27 off 49 before getting dismissed while de Zorzi followed suit scoring 30. The middle order did struggle, but Wiaan Mulder and Kyle Verreynne have been impressive and managed to extend the lead to 34 runs, and with 4 wickets still in hand, South Africa will be eying to get a lead of around 100 runs which could be massive on this pitch.

Winning the toss and choosing to bat quickly turned out to be the incorrect call for Bangladesh as they found themselves reduced to 45/5 in no time. The ball was swinging and spinning making it very difficult for the batters, but still, it wasn't a wicket where you get bowled out for 106. The only one who looked solid was the opener, Mahmudul Hasan Joy who made a gritty 30 while Mehidy Hasan and Taijul Islam contributed towards the end to get them to a three-digit total. Initially, Wiaan Mulder made the new ball talk and ended up with three wickets, while Kagiso Rabada joined the party late but got his 300th Test wicket and picked up 3 as well. Keshav Maharaj bowled brilliantly as well getting a lot of turn but had to wait for his first and then went on to get a couple more while Dane Piedt chipped in with one.

THE OFFICIAL WORD IS IN AND THAT WILL BE STUMPS ON DAY 1! A fascinating Day 1 where as many as 16 wickets fell comes to an abrupt end! Not sure whether the batters enjoyed it as much as the bowlers but Test cricket is all about challenges and how you find ways to overcome them. It was a day to remember for Kagiso Rabada and Taijul Islam as they reached personal milestones of 300 and 200 Test wickets respectively. Rabada also became the fastest ever to achieve this feat in terms of the number of balls bowled. Also, that brilliant five-for from Taijul has kept Bangladesh in this game after a disaster with the bat earlier.

The light meter is out now! The umpires think that the artificial light has taken over the natural light and it is not safe for us to continue. We can see the players making their way out of the ground now. The reading that the umpire has taken here will be used for the rest of the Test. It is not officially Stumps on Day 1, but it does not look like we will get any more action here and if that is the case, we will be losing 6 overs of play.

South Africa were rocked early losing Aiden Markram, but Tony de Zorzi has looked solid right from the start. He and Tristan Stubbs kept the game moving forward with a 41-run partnership and every run on this wicket is crucial. Stubbs was playing well but lost his focus which cost him his wicket when he was well set. David Bedingham joined Tony de Zorzi and both of them have been proactive because trying to survive on this wicket is probably not a good option. Bangladesh have bowled well, but they need wickets to get back in this game while a couple of good partnerships from Proteas will take the game away from the hosts. Join us at 9 am GMT to catch all the exciting action in the last session.

SESSION SUMMARY - 111 runs and 6 wickets in 30 overs! South Africa still holds the upper hand in this game, but this match is far from over! After being rolled over for just 106 runs, Bangladesh started well with the ball as Hasan Mahmud removed Aiden Markram in the very first over with a beauty. Batting has not been easy on this wicket as there is something for both the pacers and spinners. It is only Day 1, and we have seen the ball turn square. The hosts kept going and going, and not long before Tea, Taijul Islam was introduced and provided the breakthrough in his second over.
Short and outside off, David Bedingham waits back and cuts it to deep point for a single. That will be Tea on Day 1!

Commentary.Commentary: Full, on middle and off, Tristan Stubbs gets ahead and makes a solid block up front.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 1.3: Mehidy Hasan to Tristan Stubbs, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: Off the mark! Mehidy Hasan keeps it very short and outside off, Tony de Zorzi hangs back and cuts it hard to deep point for a single.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 1.2: Mehidy Hasan to Tony de Zorzi, 1 run.

Commentary.Commentary: Comes from around the wicket and pitches it full, on off, Tony de Zorzi drives it to cover.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 1.1: Mehidy Hasan to Tony de Zorzi, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: Tristan Stubbs walks out to bat at number 3. Also, spin from the other end as Bangladesh only has one seamer in this game. Mehidy Hasan to share the attack.

OUT! TIMBER! Hasan Mahmud has set Markram perfectly and Bangladesh get the first breakthrough that they needed! Comes from over the wicket and lands it on a good length, just outside off and gets the ball to jag back in a fair bit. Aiden Markram plays down the wrong line and gets beaten on the inside edge. The ball goes past the gap between the gap of bat and pad and hits the top of middle. South Africa lose their skipper and are 9/1 at the end of the first over.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 0.6: Hasan Mahmud to Aiden Markram, OUT! b Hasan Mahmud.

Commentary.Commentary: Great ball! Digs it in short, over off with some extra zip off the surface, Aiden Markram sways away and lets it go through!
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 0.5: Hasan Mahmud to Aiden Markram, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: Pulls the length back and attacks the pads, on a back of a length, Aiden Markram fails to tucks it across and the ball goes off his pads to deep fine for a couple more. Called leg byes!
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 0.4: Hasan Mahmud to Aiden Markram, 2 Leg byes.

Commentary.Commentary: NO BALL! Hasan Mahmud has overstepped. Not more than a whisker! Fuller in length, just outside off, Aiden Markram drives it through covers for two more runs.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 0.4: Hasan Mahmud to Aiden Markram, No ball!

Commentary.Commentary: FOUR! Aiden Markram and South Africa are underway with a boundary! Too full, outside off with a hint of away swing, Aiden Markram frees his arms and slashes at it. Gets a very thick outside edge that goes past backward point to his left for a boundary.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 0.3: Hasan Mahmud to Aiden Markram, Four!

Commentary.Commentary: A tad fuller than a good length, on off, Aiden Markram drives it well but straight to point.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 0.2: Hasan Mahmud to Aiden Markram, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: Starts right on the money does Hasan Mahmud! Comes from over the wicket and hits the good length, on off and gets the ball to straighten up off the deck to beat the outside edge as Aiden Markram looks to play at it with a straight bat. Surprisingly the ball doesn't carry to the keeper on the full.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 0.1: Hasan Mahmud to Aiden Markram, No run.
